entities.name: François Séverin Marceau
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
François Séverin Marceau-Desgraviers (1769–1796) was a French Revolutionary general renowned for rapid manoeuvre in the Vendée and on the Rhine, dying young after the Battle of Altenkirchen. Rising from volunteer ranks, he embodied the Republic’s new meritocratic officer corps against royalist and Coalition foes.

His operations with Kléber and others helped contain the Vendée before transfer to the Army of Sambre-and-Meuse, where aggressive advance made him a Republican hero. Death at twenty-seven sealed a romantic martial legend later celebrated across French memory.

Marceau remains a type of the brilliant Revolutionary captain cut short by war.
